title: Multi-instance MQ queue manager not failing over to standby node
description: We tested the MQ multi-instance failover last week by stopping the active node, and the standby node did not take over. The business continuity test failed. The standby node shows as 'Standby' in the MQ status but does not become Active.

worklogs.description: Checked the shared filesystem mount on the standby node. NFS mount is present but shows as read-only.
Investigated NFS server configuration. Export options for the MQ data share changed from rw to ro on the standby server's entry.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Hello, I investigated the failover failure. The standby node attempted to acquire the active role but could not because the shared filesystem (NFS) is mounted read-only on the standby server. The MQ data and log directories on the shared filesystem require read-write access for the standby to become active. The NFS server's export configuration was recently changed and the standby server's entry was inadvertently set to read-only. I need to work with the infrastructure team to correct the...

comments.author: customer
comments.message: That would be the storage team - contact Hakan Sahin. He set up the NFS shares when the multi-instance was deployed.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Contacting Hakan now. I have the specific NFS export entry that needs to change: the export for the standby server's IP address needs to include 'rw' instead of 'ro' in the options. I will also need the NFS service to reload its exports after the change (exportfs -r). Once done, I will re-test the failover to confirm it works correctly.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Hakan confirmed he can make the NFS export change but needs a 30-minute window to do it without affecting other NFS clients on the same server. Scheduled for today 17:00. Will retest failover at 17:30.
